name: Light Greyish Olive
lede: Light Greyish Olive is a muted, pale shade of [[olive]], traced to a 1912 Ridgway plate and found, as photographed, in one painting of our archive in nine.

sections.title: A Ridgway modifier
sections.body: The name combines the modifiers *light* and *greyish* with the base color [[olive]] [1]. It is first recorded in Robert Ridgway's 1912 *Color Standards and Nomenclature*, plate XLVI, hue 21'''', tone b, a scan of an aged plate and so only an approximation of Ridgway's original ink [1]. The ISCC-NBS lists of 1955 fold the same range into block 109, naming it "light olive gray," a Delta-E of 5.4 from this hex [1]. Nearest on file are [[olive-grey]] and [[yellow-grey]], 3.4 and 3.8 units away [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this shade, as photographed, in 2,673 of 23,781 paintings, 11.24 percent; within a single canvas it is a distinct area in 1,687 of them, more common than 94 percent of our named colors [2]. Meindert Hobbema is its most devoted painter by a wide margin, using it in 11 of 16 works here, 6.4 times the baseline rate of the museums those paintings come from [2]. It peaks in the 1900s at 8.7 percent of that century's 1,674 paintings, and inside a painting it most often plays a light, in 36 percent of its 1,687 appearances [2]. The earliest match dates to 1100, 812 years before the name's 1912 record; the archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor, not a first [2]. It shares canvases with [[beige-grey]] more often than chance, a lift of 4.1 [2].
